title: Giving in the Church
definition: Giving in the Church is the generous, cheerful, and faithful sharing of resources for worship, ministry, mercy, and mission.
summary: Giving in the Church is worshipful stewardship that supports ministry, mercy, mission, and the needs of the body.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gave Himself for us, and His grace teaches His people to give freely and joyfully.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on financial and material generosity within congregational life. Giving is not a fee for services or a way to buy favor with God; it is a cheerful response to grace. Through giving, believers participate in ministry, care for needs, and express trust in the Lord.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because money reveals worship, fear, and priorities. Churches need giving that is transparent, wise, generous, and mission-shaped. This doctrine protects giving from manipulation on one side and selfishness on the other.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Give thoughtfully, cheerfully, and sacrificially as God enables. Ask whether your resources reflect kingdom priorities. Churches should handle gifts with integrity and communicate how generosity serves ministry and mercy.
